### `scripts/fetch-osm.mjs`
Follow ARCHITECTURE §B5 exactly: the Overpass query, the retry, grouping into short names, clipping, Douglas–Peucker, 5-decimal rounding, output shape, counts, and exit 1 on a missing road or place. Use Node's built-in `fetch`. Opus confirmed the tag values in 7A (see 7A Research). Watch for two things:
- `CO 83` is a `ref` (often with no name).
- Woodmen and Garden of the Gods carry `East`/`West` prefixes.

Short-name mapping:

| OSM match | Short name | `major` |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` has `I 25` | I-25 | true |
| `ref` has `US 24` | US 24 | false |
| `ref` = `CO 83` | Hwy 83 | false |
| Academy Boulevard | Academy | false |
| Woodmen Road | Woodmen | false |
| Powers Boulevard | Powers | false |
| Garden of the Gods Road | Garden of the Gods | false |
| Austin Bluffs Parkway | Austin Bluffs | false |
| Templeton Gap Road | Templeton Gap | false |
| Baptist Road | Baptist | false |

When a way matches both a ref and a name (for example US 24 on Platte Ave), the ref wins. Keep only the attribute set described in §B5.

### `mapview.ts`
```ts
import type { BBox, ZoneCollection } from './geo.ts';
export interface View { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }   // SVG units
export interface MapFrame {
  project(lng: number, lat: number): [number, number];
  full: View;                     // 4:5, contains bboxOf(zones) padded 6%
  viewFor(box: BBox, pad?: number): View;   // 4:5, contains box padded `pad` (default 0.10), centred on it
  include(view: View, x: number, y: number, margin?: number): View; // smallest 4:5 view ⊇ view that also contains the point
}
export function makeFrame(zones: ZoneCollection): MapFrame;
export const viewBoxAttr = (v: View) => `${v.x} ${v.y} ${v.w} ${v.h}`;
```
- Projection per ARCHITECTURE §B4. `lat0` is the centre of `bboxOf(zones)`. Scale `k` puts the full view at **1000 units wide**. Round output to 0.1 units.
- `makeFrame` is deterministic: the build and the client both call it on the same `zones.geojson`, so no parameters need to pass through the DOM.

### ServiceMap
`src/components/ServiceMap.astro`, prop `focus?: ZoneKey`. All geometry is computed in the frontmatter at build time.
- Read `zones.geojson` and `osm.geojson` (`?raw` + `JSON.parse`, as book.ts does), and `makeFrame(zones)`.
- `<div class="service-map">` containing:
  - `<svg viewBox=…full or viewFor(focus)… role="img" aria-labelledby="map-title map-desc" data-full={viewBoxAttr(full)} preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">` with `<title id="map-title">` and `<desc id="map-desc">` from the copy deck.
  - Layers in the order given in ARCHITECTURE §B4. Zone fills and zone outlines are separate `<path>`s with `data-zone`, `class="zone zone--{key}"` and `class="zone-line zone-line--{key}"`. Use `fill-rule="evenodd"` so holes render.
  - Roads: one `<path class="road">` per short name, plus `road--major` for I-25. Road label `<text class="road-label">`, place `<text class="place-label">`, zone `<text class="zone-label">`. Each label's position is a `transform="translate(x y)"` on a `<g>`, so the counter-scale can be applied with CSS.
  - The pin is `<g class="map-pin" hidden><path …/></g>`: a 24×32 teardrop drawn with its tip at (0,0).
- When `focus` is a home/shared/north zone, add `is-focused` / `is-muted` classes as book.ts would and set `--map-scale` inline (`style="--map-scale: N"`). For `focus='out'` or no focus, use the full view and scale 1.
- Paths: `M`/`L` commands from projected points, with `Z` per ring for zones. Round to 0.1. **No hex.** Colours come from CSS classes using tokens (ARCHITECTURE §B4 "Styling").
- Labels:
  - Zone: pole of inaccessibility (grid search, about 40×40 over the polygon's bbox, keeping the interior point with the largest distance to any edge). Text from `site.zones[key].name`.
  - Road: a vertex near the middle of the longest line inside the full view.
  - Places: at the point, offset slightly.
  - A `labelNudge: Record<string, [number, number]>` table at the top of the frontmatter for manual fixes.
- CSS (scoped, plus `:global` where book.ts toggles classes):
  - The `svg` is `display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 4 / 5; max-width: 34rem; background: var(--bg-light); border: 1px solid var(--line-dark); border-radius: var(--radius);`.
  - Text: `font-size: calc(Npx / var(--map-scale, 1))`, using sizes in SVG units that come out at about 13px for roads and places and 15px for zones at the 34rem width.
  - Pin: `transform: translate(...) scale(calc(1 / var(--map-scale, 1)))`, set by JS as an inline style (`translate` from the projection).
  - `.is-interactive .zone { cursor: pointer }`.
- Below the svg: `<p class="map-hint" hidden>…</p>`, the credit line, and the "Open the map in Google Maps" link. The hint, credit and link use `--fs-small`.
- Draw every road and place in `osm.geojson`, with no clip to the view (Opus decision 3 under Report).
- Keep the whole inline SVG under ~40 KB. If it's bigger, raise the simplification tolerance in `fetch-osm.mjs` and re-run it.

### `book.ts`
Follow the ARCHITECTURE §B4 state machine. Specifics:
- **Places stays exactly as in 3B** (`loadPlaces`, the combobox, `unavailable()`). The map never depends on Google; there's no Maps JS map.
- **`init()`:**
  - Find `#mobile .service-map svg`. Build `frame = makeFrame(zones)`, from the zones already imported.
  - Add `is-interactive` to the svg and un-hide `.map-hint`.
  - Add one delegated click handler on `#mobile`:
    - `a[data-zone]` inside `.zone-picker`: `preventDefault()` and `select(zone, 'pick')`. Let modified clicks (ctrl, meta, shift, middle button) through.
    - `path.zone[data-zone]` in the svg: `select(zone, 'pick')`.
- **`select(zone, via, loc?)`:** replaces `showZone`.
  - Template: `template[data-zone="${zone}"][data-via="${via}"]`, else `template[data-zone="${zone}"]:not([data-via])`. Clone it into `#zone-result` and focus the heading.
  - Set `aria-current="true"` on the matching picker link and remove it from the others.
  - Call `setPin(loc ?? null)`, then `focusZone(zone)`.
  - When `via === 'pick'` and the combobox exists, clear its value and close the list.
  - Keep the DEV-only `window` hook, pointed at `select`.
- **`focusZone(zone)`:**
  - home/shared/north: `view = frame.viewFor(bboxOf(zones, zone))`; `is-focused` on that zone's fill and line, `is-muted` on the others.
  - out: `view = frame.full`, then `frame.include(view, pinX, pinY)` if the pin is set; no muting.
  - Set `svg.setAttribute('viewBox', viewBoxAttr(view))` and `svg.style.setProperty('--map-scale', String(frame.full.w / view.w))`.
- **`setPin(loc)`:** `null` → hide `.map-pin`. Otherwise `[x, y] = frame.project(lng, lat)`, then set `transform: translate(${x}px, ${y}px) scale(calc(1 / var(--map-scale)))` as an inline style and un-hide it.
  - If CSS `transform` on SVG `<g>` misbehaves in a browser you test, use the `transform` attribute with an explicit scale number instead. Report which one you used.
- **Address selection:** `select(zoneFor(lat, lng, zones), 'address', { lat, lng })`.
- **Privacy:** the pin coordinates exist only in memory and in the pin's transform. Never write them to storage, the URL, the console or text. No `console.*` anywhere.

`tests/mapview.test.ts`, using the real `zones.geojson`:
- `full.w / full.h` is 0.8 (±0.001), and `full.w` is 1000 (±0.5).
- Every projected zone vertex lies inside `full`.
- For each zone, `viewFor(bboxOf(zones, z))` is 4:5 and contains all of that zone's projected vertices.
- `include(full, x, y)` with a point far east is 4:5 and contains both the old view and the point.
- `project` is monotonic: east → larger x, north → smaller y.

`tests/osm.test.ts`: `src/data/osm.geojson` has every short name from the table and the 7 places (including `Security-Widefield`). Feature properties are only `kind`, `name` and (for roads) `major`. All coordinates lie in the §B5 box `38.63,-105.09,39.17,-104.54` (S,W,N,E).

### Deviations
1. **Pin drawn at 2.25×.** The 24×32 teardrop came out 8×10px on a 343px-wide map, too small to see. `ServiceMap` wraps the glyph in `<g transform="scale(2.25)">` (tip still at 0,0; the JS is as specified) and `PIN_MARGIN` in `book.ts` is 100 (it was 60) because the glyph is about 72 units tall.
2. **Header breakpoints.** Compact type: `max-width: 29rem` → `33rem` (the full-size row needs about 520px). Icon-only logo: `22.5rem` → `25rem` (compact row plus the 110px logo needs about 391px). At 375px the nav overflowed before this.
3. **Label sizes are tiered by viewport**, not one size: `--t-road`/`--t-zone` are 34/38 below 24rem, 30/34 from 24rem, 26/30 from 30rem and 24/28 from 36rem (the step's sizes apply from 36rem up). Below that the map is only about 340px wide, so the step's sizes came out near 8px.
4. **Extra attributes:** `data-zone` on zone outlines and zone labels (so `focusZone` can toggle them), and `data-road` on road paths.
5. **Test setup.** Port 4321 was held by an `astro preview` of `dist/` (pid 32024, started Oct 5), so a dev server there wasn't possible. I ran my own dev server on 4322 for layout work and used the preview on 4321, rebuilt, for the Google Places checks (the key referrer is 4321 only). I stopped an old dev server (pid 13932) and the one I started; **the preview is still running**.

### Observations for 7R (not changed)
- **Swatch vs map colour.** The map fills are `--zone-*` at 0.35 opacity, so they look pale. The button swatches use the full colour. The Central & Southwest swatch (`--green-700` on a `--green-900` button) reads as almost empty. "The colors match the area buttons" is only roughly true.
- **Desktop layout.** The map is 34rem wide and left-aligned, so about half the row is empty at 1280px.
- **Mobile.** After choosing an area the card pushes the map below the first screen (the §B4 order). After zooming to one zone, the other zones are mostly off the visible map, so on the map you can only click the zone you're in; the buttons still work.
- **OSM joins.** Two short, isolated diagonal line fragments show inside the map (roughly mid-Central & Southwest, and just north of Woodmen on the left). They look like stray short ways rather than a bad join. I didn't change the join logic.
- **`Colorado Springs` label** is nudged 75 units south of its OSM point to clear the Central label, so it reads as a name, not a location.
- The terracotta focus ring shows around the card heading after JS focus (existing behaviour).
